newsitem.title: UK: Euro Crude Outlook - Few obstacles to further fall.
newsitem.headline: Euro Crude Outlook - Few obstacles to further fall.

text.p: European benchmark crude Dated Brent is set for further falls this week with local fundamentals weak and opportunities for trans-Atlantic sales limited by competing West African barrels, traders said.

Wet Brent values slid by nearly 50 cents last week, tumbling to July Brent -30 cents on Friday from what most traders agreed were artificial highs reached on the back of aggressive trading house buying.
"It's going to get weaker...it has some way to go," said one North Sea trader.
Poor refining margins which forced run cuts at the major Rotterdam refineries in the second half of May has suppressed the appetites of the North Sea crude market's key buyers.

While lower throughputs boosted profit margins by $1.00 a barrel to over $2.00 at a complex Rotterdam refinery last week, crude buyers are still cautious with July North Sea production set to jump after heavy field maintenance in June.
"No-one wants to buy in a falling market. All the bullish news like the June North Sea shutdowns is out of the way," a trader said.
Other North Sea grades held steady as Brent hurtled lower.
But some traders expected them to ease this week.
"If Brent falls they'll follow suit. The differentials are too strong," said one.
While a trans-Atlantic arbitrage usually offers a natural floor in a falling wet Brent market, traders said that West African barrels may prove more attractive to U.S. refiners.
"The arb is further away than you think," a trader said.
A widening Brent/Dubai spread is to blame with West African cargoes earmarked for the Far East set to go to the U.S. Gulf.
Last week, Indian Oil Corp picked up only two Dubai cargoes in its monthly buying tender.
That left a further five scrambling for homes and deflating quotes on the Dubai paper market.
The July/August Dubai intermonth spread slipped 15 cents late last week pulling the Brent/Dubai differential wider.

A narrow Brent-Dubai spread encouraged heavy chartering of West African crude to the Far East earlier in the month, but the cargoes found themselves in an oversupplied market with no room for local grades.
"It's an unsustainable situation with the East exporting local grades to the (U.S.) Gulf Coast and importing West Africana," trader said.
"The West African barrels are going to be switched to the U.S. Gulf."
In the Mediterranean, sour crude buyers are waiting for news of whether the U.N. intended to renew the Iraqi oil-for-food deal for a further six months. The agreement expires on June 9.

They said a rollover would lend a bearish sentiment to the market but an expected lull in fresh Iraqi exports means that slim refining margins will serve as a more immediate cap to the sour market. Regional benchmark Russian Urals was unlikely to climb above Dated Brent -$1.30/$1.25, they said.
